text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Communist Party chief Do Muoi has called for an intensification of ideological and cultural activities.
-- The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) is seeking to strengthen cultural and information cooperation with Vietnam.
-- Two major heroin dens have been discovered in Ho Chi Minh City.
-- ASEAN will admit Laos, Cambodia and Burma at the same time later this year.
-- Vietnam and India have signed accords on environment, trade, finance and investment protection and encouragement.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet arrived in Bangladesh on Sunday for the first high-ranking visit since 1973.
-- Foreign investors have earmarked $8.317 billion towards 515 projects in Ho Chi Minh City so far.
-- Hanoi's municipal authorities have announced compulsory labour plans for city residents.
-- Some 5,283 HIV carriers have been identified in Vietnam so far. 82.5 percent are between the ages of 30 and 49, and 0.3 percent under 13.
-- Thai Foreign Minister Prachuab Chaiyasarn will arrive in Hanoi on March 12 for a three-day official visit.
-- Hanoi plans a $650 million international mini-city on the outskirts of the capital.
